title: Rust client
what: The service's Rust client: one blocking call per route in the wire types, sending the bearer token on every call (src/client.rs).

title: Background clocks
what: The daemon's own clocks: the transcript scan, the event-log prune and the ten-minute alive line, each on a thread of its own (src/clocks.rs).

title: Configuration
what: The JSON config file read once at start over the defaults, and the three keys behind the live settings that a settings change merges back into it (src/config.rs).

title: HTTP server
what: The daemon's routes: health, the events and their stream, the stats, the settings and the siren test behind the bearer token, and the pages outside it (src/server.rs).

title: Structured log
what: The daemon's log file and the one-line format its entries are written in, echoed to standard output unless quiet (src/log.rs).

title: OpenAPI document
what: The OpenAPI 3.1 document generated from the wire types, the routes and the MCP tools, kept as docs/openapi.json and held to the code by a test (src/openapi.rs).

title: Data directory and paths
what: The data directory and the files in it, and the home-based default paths for transcripts and data the siren uses (src/data_dir.rs, src/paths.rs).

title: Time
what: Epoch seconds and milliseconds, and the host-local reading of a transcript's timestamps (src/clock.rs).

title: Bearer token
what: The bearer token every API route takes, read from its file and written with a new random one, readable by its user alone, when the file is missing (src/token.rs).

title: Wire bodies
what: The bodies the API takes and answers in the common wire format: usages, events, pages, stats, settings and the siren, with their JSON Schemas (src/wire.rs).
